images.title: Circles on a base of 8
images.purpose: Show circles of radius 4 and 5 on an 8 cm base, with X and BX, so the crossing is visible.
images.composition: A horizontal base across the middle with two overlapping circles, the overlap lens clearly visible.
exact_structure: A horizontal teal (#0072B2) segment AB labelled 8 cm, dots at A (left end) and B (right end).
A full amber (#E69F00) circle centred at A with radius 4 cm, meeting AB at its midpoint X.
A full reddish purple (#CC79A7) circle centred at B with radius 5 cm, reaching 1 cm past X toward A, so the circles overlap in a lens that is 1 cm wide along AB.
Point X is marked with a dot and the label X at the exact midpoint of AB.
A thin grey (#6B7280) bracket labelled BX = 4 cm under the right half of AB, and radii marked 4 cm on the amber circle and 5 cm on the purple circle.
The circles cross at exactly two points, one above and one below AB, each marked with a small dot.
rejection: circles that touch or cross at only one point
the circle at B not reaching past X
X not at the midpoint of AB
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The circle at B has radius 5, longer than BX = 4, so it enters the circle at A and the circles cross twice.
images.description: Circles of radius 4 at A and 5 at B on an 8 cm base crossing at two points.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Compare the radius 5 with BX = 4 to see the circle at B must go past X.

image_decisions.why: This is the key picture for why a triangle with sides 4, 5 and 8 exists.
